correctness.rationale: Build graph from five cycle edges, ten shadow-to-neighbor edges and five apex-shadow edges; unique vertex degree classes (4,3,5) establish D5 as full automorphism group. Exhaust all 2^11=2048 initial blue subsets with synchronous forcing and independently implemented sequential closure (each step strictly increases blue count, so termination and exhaustive correctness). Exactly 175 size-five sets are successful and none of cardinality<5; all polynomial coefficients follow. Partition 175 optimum masks under 10 D5 actions to 16 size-ten and 3 size-five orbits. Exchange adjacency is |symmetric difference|=2; two independent edge-generation procedures give 1180 edges. BFS from each of 175 exchange vertices gives distances (1180,4780,6445,2610,210), radius4, diameter5, and pair total choose(175,2). Independent code reproduced entire exhaustive finite calculation; this genuinely exhausts all graph states, unlike partial samples.

value.rationale: The Grötzsch graph is a canonical smallest triangle-free 4-chromatic graph. Its complete zero-forcing polynomial, all minimum-set orbits and the connected reconfiguration metric are mathematically motivated exact invariants, not an arbitrary tiny example. A complete finite 2048-state enumeration legitimately proves a whole finite classification; a researcher interested in propagation, zero-forcing polynomials or reconfiguration can need these exact counts. Scalar Z(G)=5 alone may already be known.

limitations: One specific 11-vertex graph; token jumping not token sliding; no general infinite family formula.
